acceptance_criteria.criterion: New run with UUID collision regenerates a new UUID and logs a warning
Resuming a terminal checkpoint prints clear warning and exits non-zero
Resuming a non-terminal checkpoint works normally (no regression)
Unit tests cover both new-run collision and terminal-resume scenarios

summary: Added three checkpoint helper functions to cli.py: _thread_id_exists_in_checkpoint (stdlib sqlite3 query), _mark_run_terminal (writes {thread_id}.terminal marker file), _is_run_terminal (checks marker file).

Modified thread ID generation: new runs check for UUID collision in the SQLite DB and regenerate up to 5 times (log.warning on each collision); resume runs check for terminal marker and exit EXIT_ERROR with a clear diagnostic message.
After a successful non-interrupted graph.ainvoke call, _mark_run_terminal is called to record the run as complete.
Added 12 new unit tests across 4 test classes: TestThreadIdExistsInCheckpoint, TestMarkAndIsRunTerminal, TestTerminalResumeGuard, TestUuidCollisionHandling. All 46 CLI tests pass.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/cli.py — _mark_run_terminal is not called when --interrupt-on is active, so a run that was previously interrupted and then resumed to completion would never be marked terminal. If resuming interrupted runs to their natural end is a use case, the terminal marker logic should also run in the resume path when interrupt_before is empty.

orchestrator/src/cli.py — The .terminal marker files accumulate in the checkpoint_dir indefinitely; no cleanup mechanism exists. At scale this could produce orphaned files. Consider a periodic sweep or linking the marker lifetime to the SQLite checkpoint lifecycle.

summary: Reviewed WP-004: UUID collision guard and terminal resume guard in orchestrator/src/cli.py.
_thread_id_exists_in_checkpoint: stdlib sqlite3 (no LangGraph dep), parameterized query (SQL injection safe), defensive except Exception: return False. Correct.
_mark_run_terminal: mkdir(parents, exist_ok), .touch(), silent OSError suppression. Correct.
UUID collision guard: correctly skips DB query if file absent. Loop limit of 5 prevents infinite loop. Minor off-by-one on last iteration (5th regenerated UUID unchecked) — statistically irrelevant.
Terminal resume guard: correct error message with actionable guidance, returns EXIT_ERROR. Guard is checked before MCP startup, which is the right fail-fast location.
_mark_run_terminal correctly placed behind 'if not interrupt_before:' — interrupted runs remain resumable, which is the intended behavior.
All 4 ACs verified through QA. Two low-priority improvement observations recorded but neither blocks PASS.

comments.note: The UUID collision loop (for _ in range(5)) generates a new UUID at the end of each failing iteration but does not re-check that UUID before the next loop iteration starts. After 5 consecutive collisions, the 5th regenerated UUID is used without a final existence check. Statistically irrelevant given UUID v4's 2^122 space, but could be tightened by checking at the top of each iteration (e.g. while _thread_id_exists_in_checkpoint(...): for _ in range(5): ... else: log.error(...)).

The except Exception block in _thread_id_exists_in_checkpoint silently returns False without any log entry. If a DB I/O error occurs during a new run, the collision check silently passes and the run proceeds. This is the correct defensive behavior, but adding log.debug('Skipping checkpoint collision check due to DB error: %s', exc) would make the suppression visible in debug logs and ease troubleshooting.
